item.title: Tight Bounds for Paging with Time Windows and Joint Replenishment with Varying Opening Costs
item.description: arXiv:2610.30430v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the paging with time windows problem, a natural generalization of classical paging, in which each request must be served within a specified time interval. This model allows the algorithm to delay service and batch service requests over time, but also introduces significant challenges due to overlapping requests. While the problem is well understood in the unweighted setting, where optimal $O(\log k)$-competitive algorithms are known, the weighted case remains more elusive. The best previously known algorithm, due to Gupta, Kumar, and Panigrahi, achieves an $O(\log k \log n)$-competitive ratio, leaving a gap between weighted and unweighted settings. We obtain an $O(\log k)$-competitive algorithm for weighted paging with time windows, matching the optimal competitive ratio. The core of our approach is a structural decomposition that separates the evolution of the cache from the scheduling of page loads. We show that, given a sequence of cache configurations, computing a near-optimal sequence of page loads reduces to a variant of the Joint Replenishment Problem with deadlines (JRP-D) with time-dependent opening costs. We design a constant-competitive online algorithm for this variant and prove that the reduction is tight. Combining this with an existing online construction of cache configurations yields the desired bound.
item.dc:creator: Joseph Seffi Naor, Tomer Tsachor

item.title: The Cost of Missed States: Online Tracking with Current-Observation Resets
item.description: arXiv:2610.30505v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An online tracker retains one state and may reset only to the current observation, although its complete observed history is available. Offline knows the future and obeys the same reset rule. Under a hard discrepancy radius, for every horizon $T\ge5$ and every feasible randomized causal policy, a fixed path on a known five-point metric requires at least $(T+1)/2$ expected refreshes, against exactly two offline refreshes with a strict radius margin. Missing the useful prefix center forces a refresh at every suffix observation. The path visits four values, with resolution fixed as $T$ grows. Write $J_\lambda$ for cumulative discrepancy plus a charge $\lambda>0$ per refresh, and $V_T$ for the sum of successive observation distances. A candidate prefix adapts Bienkowski and Schmid's randomized lower bound to this objective under current resets, even with a known horizon and $V_T<3\lambda$. This construction needs finer grids; a fixed finite metric with positive minimum separation instead admits a competitive policy for penalized tracking. An anytime policy satisfies $J_\lambda\le\lambda+4\sqrt{\lambda TV_T}$ without knowing the horizon or final variation. Clipping for a known horizon gives $J_\lambda\le\lambda T$ and a factor-three comparison with the minimum of three analytical bounds, without knowing final variation. Current-value diameter and readout sensitivity give same-input output bounds for mixtures, including squared-distance softmax.
item.dc:creator: Hiroyasu Usami

item.title: Optimal Mixing for Local Edge-Coloring Dynamics on Trees
item.description: arXiv:2610.30625v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the mixing time of two local Markov chains for uniformly sampling proper edge colorings of trees. For a tree with $n$ vertices and maximum degree $\Delta$, we establish optimal mixing-time bounds for the single-edge Glauber dynamics when $q\ge\Delta+2$ and for the neighboring-edge heat-bath dynamics when $q\ge\Delta+1$. Both chains mix in $O_\Delta(n(\log n+\log(1/\varepsilon)))$ steps, uniformly over the number of colors $q$. These bounds are tight in their dependence on $n$ for fixed $\Delta$. Our proof establishes log-Sobolev inequalities through local color release, reusable recoloring buffers, and component entropy mixing. The two dynamics require different local constructions: a two-spare-color buffer for single-edge updates and a second-layer controller for neighboring-edge updates. The resulting entropy analysis applies to general bounded-degree trees, including regimes where worst-case spatial mixing fails.
item.dc:creator: Haoran wang

item.title: Near-Quadratic Time Multivariate Polynomial Interpolation
item.description: arXiv:2610.30907v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\F$ be a finite field. Given $N$ distinct points $\bm{\alpha}_1,\ldots,\bm{\alpha}_N \in \F^m$ and associated values $\beta_1,\ldots,\beta_N \in \F$, we study the problem of computing an $m$-variate polynomial $f(\vy) \in \F[\vy]$ of individual degree less than $d$, with $d^m \ge N$, that satisfies $f(\bm{\alpha}_i)=\beta_i$ for all $i\in[N]$, whenever such an $f$ exists. This is known as the\textit{ multivariate polynomial interpolation} problem. In this work, given $N=d^m$, we present a deterministic algorithm for multivariate polynomial interpolation over an arbitrary finite field $\F$ that runs in near-quadratic time $N^{2+o(1)}\poly(m,d,\log|\F|)$, assuming $d$ is $\omega(1)$. This bound holds whenever the associated \emph{multivariate Vandermonde} matrix is nonsingular, has constant co-rank, or admits some special structure. In the general case, we give a randomized Las Vegas algorithm attaining the same near-quadratic running time, provided the finite field is sufficiently large and $d$ grows similar to the previous case. Unlike other multivariate interpolation strategies, we do not assume black-box access to the polynomial. In particular, we are not permitted to query arbitrary input points to obtain their evaluations. Our interpolation result follows by combining Wiedemann's classical approach~\cite{w86} for solving sparse linear systems with known bounds for fast \emph{multivariate multipoint evaluation} over finite fields~\cite{umans08, KU11, BGKM23, BGGKU24}. Specifically, our deterministic interpolation strategy relies on a deterministic variant of Wiedemann's approach, which is more commonly used in the randomized setting.
item.dc:creator: Chandra Kanta Mohapatra

item.title: Pigeonhole Equal Subset Sum: Subexponential Algorithm, Tight Lower Bounds, and Average-Case Analysis
item.description: arXiv:2610.31056v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Equal Subset Sum problem asks, given n positive integers bounded by M, to find two distinct non-empty subsets with the same sum. We study this problem in the regime $M = 2^{o(n)}$, where the pigeonhole principle guarantees that a solution exists, and the main challenge is to find one efficiently. A straightforward dynamic-programming algorithm runs in time poly(n).$M$. After a sequence of improvements, the current best algorithm, due to Jin, Williams, and Zhang (ESA 2025), achieves running time poly(n).$M^{1/3}$. In this work, we give the first poly(n).$M^{o(1)}$-time algorithm for Equal Subset Sum in the regime $M = 2^{o(n)}$. We complement this algorithmic result with a tight conditional lower bound showing that any substantial improvement would require a major breakthrough in approximation algorithms for lattice problems, building on recent techniques of Vafa and Vaikuntanathan (STOC 2025). Finally, we show that our techniques yield an asymptotically faster algorithm for the regime when $M = \Theta(2^{n})$: a poly(n)$\cdot 2^{n/4}$-time algorithm in the average case.
item.dc:creator: Deepak Bhati, Pranjal Dutta, Antoine Joux, Mahesh Sreekumar Rajasree, Karol Wegrzycki

item.title: Iterative Randomized Rounding for Better-Than-2 k-Median Approximation
item.description: arXiv:2610.31229v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the classic $k$-median problem and refine the iterative rounding framework recently introduced by Byrka, Guo, Hu, Li, Wan, and Wang [FOCS'26], which yields a $(2+\varepsilon)$-approximation. Our algorithm opens $k+O(1)$ facilities and achieves an expected connection cost of at most $1.9999$ times the value of the standard LP relaxation. Although the numerical improvement over $2$ is small, it establishes a conceptual result: the integrality gap of the standard relaxation is strictly below $2$ when a constant number of extra facilities is allowed. This partially answers an open question of Li and Svensson [STOC'13]. Combined with their reduction, our result yields a $1.9999$-approximation algorithm for $k$-median. Our approach builds on several technical ingredients. First, we develop a preprocessing routine that makes the LP solution $\mathrm{poly}(\varepsilon)$-integral, at the cost of a $(1+\varepsilon)$ factor in the connection cost and $O(1)$ extra facilities. Unlike the preprocessing of Byrka et al. [FOCS'26], our conversion is unconditional: it requires no special treatment of clients whose fractional facilities are concentrated. Next, we show that the main rounding algorithm can open facilities one at a time, eliminating the batch processing used by Byrka et al. [FOCS'26]. Finally, the improvement over 2 comes from a tighter analysis for clients whose distances from to its facilities are not all equal, and a complementary algorithm for the case in which these distances are nearly uniform.
item.dc:creator: Jaros{\l}aw Byrka, Yuhao Guo, Yang Hu, Shi Li, Yongho Shin, Phanu Vajanopath, Chengzhang Wan, Zaixuan Wang

item.title: A Polynomial-Time Algorithm for $k$-Path Vertex Cover Reconfiguration on Trees under Token Sliding
item.description: arXiv:2610.31261v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A $k$-path vertex cover ($k$-PVC) of a graph is a set of vertices meeting every path on $k$ vertices. In Token Sliding, one token occupies each vertex of a cover; a move slides one token along an edge to an unoccupied vertex, preserving the cover property. We study whether two covers of a tree are joined by such moves. The case $k=2$ admits a linear-time decision algorithm. For every integer $k\geq2$, we give an $O(kn^2)$-time decision algorithm on trees of order $n$, with $k$ part of the input. Two covers are reachable precisely when their rigid tokens, which never move, occupy the same set and every component remaining after their deletion has the same token count. The proof transforms configurations of equal size without rigid tokens into a canonical configuration built on properly rooted subtrees, whose paths on $k$ vertices pass through their roots. A rooted-subtree recurrence identifies movable candidate tokens. We also give a direct recursive construction between the supplied endpoints, returning at most $8n^2\,3^{\lceil n/2\rceil}$ slides in $O(n^{10}3^{n/2})$ time. ChatGPT 6 Pro and Claude Fable 5.1 were used to assist with developing and reviewing mathematical arguments and drafting and revising the paper. The author takes full responsibility for the correctness and content of the paper.
item.dc:creator: Duc A. Hoang

item.title: Kempe Reachability with $k\geq 3$ Colors Is $\mathsf{PSPACE}$-Complete on Claw-Free Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.31263v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A \emph{proper vertex coloring} assigns colors to vertices so that adjacent vertices have distinct colors. A \emph{Kempe change} in a proper vertex coloring exchanges two colors on one component of the subgraph induced by the vertices of those colors. For a fixed palette of $k$ colors, \textsc{Kempe Reachability} asks whether two given proper vertex colorings of the same graph are connected by a sequence of Kempe changes. This problem is known to be $\mathsf{PSPACE}$-complete for every fixed $k\geq 3$. A graph is \emph{claw-free} if no vertex has three pairwise nonadjacent neighbors. The \emph{line graph} of a graph has one vertex for each edge, with two vertices adjacent exactly when the corresponding edges share an end. Line graphs are claw-free, and their Kempe changes correspond to \emph{edge-Kempe changes} in the original graph, which exchange two colors on one component of the subgraph formed by the edges of those colors. A claw-free graph with a proper $k$-coloring has maximum degree at most $2k-2$, whereas for $k\geq 4$ all proper $k$-colorings of a graph of maximum degree at most $k$ are connected by Kempe changes. We show that, for every fixed $k\geq 3$, \textsc{Kempe Reachability} with $k$ colors is $\mathsf{PSPACE}$-complete even on line graphs of connected simple $k$-regular graphs, and hence even on connected $(2k-2)$-regular claw-free graphs. Equivalently, deciding whether two proper $k$-edge-colorings are connected by edge-Kempe changes is $\mathsf{PSPACE}$-complete even on connected simple $k$-regular graphs. ChatGPT 6 Pro and Claude Fable 5.1 were used to assist with developing and reviewing mathematical arguments and drafting and revising the paper. The author takes full responsibility for the correctness and content of the paper.
item.dc:creator: Duc A. Hoang

item.title: Hardness and Approximation for Compressing Deterministic Finite Automata
item.description: arXiv:2610.31273v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The delayed deterministic finite automaton ($\text{D}^2\text{FA}$) is a powerful tool for compressing the prohibitively large deterministic finite automata (DFAs) used in modern signature-based deep packet inspection systems. A $\text{D}^2\text{FA}$ augments a DFA with unlabeled default transitions to remove transitions that are similar. This technique works well in practice and has inspired numerous subsequent studies. However, existing approaches do not guarantee a $\text{D}^2\text{FA}$ of optimal size as they restrict the default transitions to form a forest. In this paper, we consider the problem of finding an optimal $\text{D}^2\text{FA}$. We make the key observation that cycles of default transitions can be valid and produce a smaller $\text{D}^2\text{FA}$, provided that for every character in the alphabet, at least one state in the cycle has an outgoing transition labeled by that character. This observation raises fundamental questions concerning the computational complexity of finding an optimal $\text{D}^2\text{FA}$ and the approximation guarantee of the standard (forest-restricted) approach. We answer both questions by showing that it is NP-hard to find an optimal $\text{D}^2\text{FA}$ and by proving that the standard approach provides a $3/2$-approximation to the optimum. To establish NP-hardness, we construct a reduction from set cover using a DFA with gadgets where valid default transition choices correspond to selecting sets. To prove our approximation ratio, we compare the cycles in an optimal solution to a variant where the default transitions form a forest. Finally, we demonstrate that this $3/2$ ratio is tight via a constructed family of DFAs.
item.dc:creator: Philip Bille, Inge Li G{\o}rtz, Christoffer Krogh, Christian M{\o}ller Mikkelstrup

item.title: A Sharp Analysis of Fixed Offset Hash Tables
item.description: arXiv:2610.31363v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the class of open addressing hash tables that uses a fixed offset sequence $r_0,r_1,\ldots,r_{n-1}$ to find an open slot in the table. As special cases this subsumes linear probing ($r_i=i$) and quadratic probing ($r_i=i^2$). We give a simple analysis that the expected insertion time when the load factor is $1-\epsilon$ is $O(\epsilon^{-2})$. This bound is tight for linear probing (but not for quadratic probing), so the analysis cannot be improved at this level of generality.
item.dc:creator: Yuhao Guo, Seth Pettie, Chengzhang Wan

item.title: Peak-Aware One-Way Trading: Competitive and Learning-Augmented Algorithms for Energy Procurement
item.description: arXiv:2610.31447v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce peak-aware one-way trading ($\texttt{PA-OWT}$), an online problem in which a player must purchase a fixed quantity of an asset by a deadline, minimizing its total cost plus a charge proportional to the largest single purchase at any time. The model is motivated by electricity procurement, where the cost of energy rewards buying at low prices, but peak demand charges discourage concentrating purchases in short periods. Balancing these incentives is challenging when future prices are unknown: a large purchase can establish a peak that later decisions cannot undo. We develop a peak-aware online algorithm that balances price and peak control with deadline feasibility and achieves the order-optimal competitive ratio. We further extend our results to a learning-augmented algorithm that uses predictions of optimal purchasing decisions to achieve an order-optimal consistency-robustness tradeoff, exploiting accurate advice while retaining worst-case guarantees in the face of arbitrary prediction errors. Finally, we evaluate our algorithms in a case study on electricity procurement using historical electricity price traces to understand the benefits of peak-aware purchasing.
item.dc:creator: Jackson Bibbens, Adam Lechowicz, Nicolas Christianson, Bo Sun, Mohammad Hajiesmaili

item.title: Coresets for $k$-Means: When Does Uniform Sampling Suffice?
item.description: arXiv:2610.31491v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Data summarization techniques, such as coresets, are essential for scaling clustering algorithms to massive datasets. We study uniform sampling, which is an extremely simple and ultra-efficient method to construct coresets, in the context of weak, stable, and strong coresets for the $k$-means problem in Hilbert space. We begin with the fundamental case $k=1$, and establish matching upper and lower bounds on the sample complexity of stable and weak coresets, finding that the two notions require different sample complexities. As a consequence, we obtain tight bounds for stable $1$-median coresets in $\ell_1$ and $\ell_2$ (and thus also Kendall--tau and Jaccard metrics), removing the dimension dependence of Carmel and Krauthgamer (ICLR 2026). Our analysis is substantially simpler than prior work and reduces to bounding the deviation of the sample mean. For the general $k$-means problem on $\rho$-separated instances, a well-studied structural assumption on the input, we show that uniform sampling yields a stable coreset for all $O(1)$-approximate solutions, and a strong coreset if the instance additionally has bounded kurtosis. In all these results, the sample complexity is independent of the dimension and the instance size.
item.dc:creator: Amir Carmel, Robert Krauthgamer

item.title: Closing All-Exp Gaps in Local Search for the Traveling Salesman Problem and Maximum Constraint Assignment
item.description: arXiv:2610.31513v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the all-exp property for the Traveling Salesman Problem with the $2$-opt neighborhood, and for $(3,2,2)$- and $(2,3,2)$-Maximum Constraint Assignment with the flip neighborhood. The all-exp property states that infinitely many instances have an initial solution from which every sequence of improving moves to a local optimum, and hence every run of local search, has exponential length. For the Traveling Salesman Problem, the all-exp property was previously known for every $k$-opt neighborhood with $k \ge 3$, so our result for $2$-opt completes the picture for all $k$-kopt neighborhoods. In $(p,q,r)$-Maximum Constraint Assignment, each constraint involves at most $p$ variables, each variable occurs in at most $q$ constraints, and each domain has size $r$. Decreasing any of the parameters of $(3,2,2)$ or $(2,3,2)$ yields a problem in which every sequence of improving flips has polynomial length, so both Maximum Constraint Assignment results are tight. All three results settle long-standing open problems. Our proofs build on a common construction idea, which reveals a close connection between the local-search dynamics of the three problems.
item.dc:creator: Sophia Heimann, Hung P. Hoang, Stefan Hougardy

item.title: Polynomial pathwidth for graphs vertex-coverable by few shortest paths and algorithms for quasi-shortest path covers
item.description: arXiv:2610.30458v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study how covering a graph by a small number of shortest or approximately shortest paths/walks constrains its treewidth and pathwidth. A path or walk is $(\alpha,\beta)$-quasi-shortest for $\alpha\geq1$ and $\beta\geq 0$ if each contiguous segment has length at most $\alpha$ times the distance between its endpoints plus $\beta$. For graphs vertex-covered by $k$ shortest paths, we establish the first known polynomial pathwidth bound of $O(k^3)$. For edge-coverage, we improve the previously known $O(k^4)$ upper bound to $O(k^2\log k)$. As a main ingredient of the proofs, we first show that if the vertices of a graph can be covered by $k$ $(\alpha,\beta)$-quasi-shortest paths or walks, then its treewidth is $O_{\alpha,\beta}(k^2)$; this is a consequence of the fact that such graphs have linear metric growth and the technique developed in [Campbell et al., E-JC 2023]. To obtain the above pathwidth upper bounds, we combine this result with techniques from the literature in a nontrivial way. On the other hand, we show that there exist connected bipartite cubic graph whose edges can be covered by $k$ shortest paths and whose pathwidth is $\Omega(k\log k)$, providing the first superlinear lower bound. For graphs covered by $k=2$ $(\alpha,0)$-quasi-shortest paths with $\alpha>1$, we show that, unlike treewidth and unlike the case $\alpha=1$ and $\beta=0$ of exact shortest paths, the pathwidth may be unbounded. Finally, for every fixed rationals $\alpha\geq1$ and $\beta\geq 0$, we give XP algorithms with a running time of $n^{f(k,\alpha,\beta)}$ for some function~$f$ that decide whether the vertices of a graph can be covered by at most $k$ $(\alpha,\beta)$-quasi-shortest paths or walks. The algorithms combine our treewidth upper bounds with an algorithmic meta-theorem from [Dreier et al., LICS 2025]. [abstract shortened to meet the arXiv requirements]
item.dc:creator: Li-Hsuan Chen, Florent Foucaud, Ling-Ju Hung, Ralf Klasing, Lucas Lorieau, Peter Rossmanith

item.title: Truthful by Omission: Click Thinning for LLM-Native Advertising
item.description: arXiv:2610.30999v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Generative AI assistants are becoming an advertising medium, embedding sponsored content in their answers. This setting departs from classical position auctions in two ways: an ad's click-through rate depends on the passage that hosts it, and because users stop at their first click, earlier ads take clicks from later ones. This competition for clicks makes truthfulness delicate: a higher bid can reshape the allocation and put a competitor ahead of the bidder, reducing the bidder's clicks. Existing mechanisms either attain a constant fraction of the optimal welfare (advertisers' total click value) but are not known to be truthful, or are truthful but their welfare guarantee degrades as the number of passages grows. We achieve both even when the answer and its editorial order are fixed before bidding. Assuming each ad's click-through rate when reached is known and unaffected by omitting other ads, we give a computationally efficient mechanism that is truthful in expectation and attains at least half the optimal welfare under free reordering. Our key idea, click thinning, omits ads at random, showing earlier ads less often so that each ad's overall click probability no longer depends on the order of the ads. Welfare maximization then reduces to a tractable matching problem, and solving it exactly with VCG-style payments makes truthful bidding optimal in expectation. Characterizing the click probabilities that omission can achieve sharpens the approximation factor from $2$ to $2-(1-\delta)^{K-1}$ when at most $K$ ads are shown and each click-through rate is at most $\delta$. This factor is the best possible for any order-preserving rule, even one that ignores incentives and computation, so truthfulness and computational efficiency incur no additional worst-case loss.
item.dc:creator: Junhua Liu, Zhicheng Liang, Zejun Zhang, Langzhou He, Feng Qian

item.title: Almost tight distributed approximation for domination in sparse graph classes
item.description: arXiv:2610.31203v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study distributed approximation of Minimum Dominating Set in a very general class of sparse graphs, extending near-optimal approximation results from the minor-free setting to bounded expansion. In more detail, for fixed $d$ and $\varepsilon>0$, we give a new deterministic constant-round LOCAL algorithm for Minimum Dominating Set on graphs of maximum average degree at most $d$ and bounded depth-one shallow-minor density. Its approximation ratio is $d+1+\varepsilon$, which is optimal up to $\varepsilon$ for every even integer $d\geq 2$. This improves on the recent results of Amiri and Siebertz by extending beyond proper minor-closed classes. From this algorithm, we derive almost-tight constant-round approximations for a number of graph classes. We get $(7+\varepsilon)$-approximations for planar graphs and graphs of bounded Euler genus, and $(5+\varepsilon)$-approximations for their triangle-free subclasses. This answers the $7+\varepsilon$ question of Wawrzyniak positively, and matches the recent results of Amiri and Siebertz. We also apply our algorithm to classes of bounded queue-number or stack-number, obtaining bounds that are tight up to $\varepsilon$. Additionally, we answer questions of Amiri and Siebertz about improving the dependence of the round complexity on $1/\varepsilon$ and obtaining polynomial local computation for fixed parameters, when comparing the output to the usual domination number.
item.dc:creator: Timoth\'e Picavet

item.title: Pipelining vs. Combining in Aggregation Tasks
item.description: arXiv:2610.31383v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the aggregation task (convergecast) in networks in the case that the values to be aggregated do not fit in a single message. We assume that every node starts with an input value, and there is an aggregation operator that is commutative, associative, and length-preserving, i.e., the result of aggregating two values has the same length as each of the input values. Since values do not fit in a message, they are transferred in a ``train'' of pipelined messages, which must be terminated whenever we want to aggregate values. The goal is to minimize the makespan time of aggregating all values. We present general lower bounds on the problem and optimal algorithms for several prevalent parallel computing architectures, including the hypercube and complete bipartite graphs, under both the splittable and unsplittable flows models. We also present an $O(\log n)$ approximation for general graphs in the unsplittable flows model.
item.dc:creator: Gabriel Marques Domingues, Claire Mathieu, Boaz Patt-Shamir

item.title: Efficient and Optimal Learning of Discrete Distributions with Person-Level Privacy
item.description: arXiv:2610.31612v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study learning a discrete distribution under person-level differential privacy in the batched setting. Given $n$ users, each contributing $m$ i.i.d. samples from an unknown distribution $\mu$ over $[k]$, we seek an estimate of $\mu$ with total-variation error $\alpha$. We give polynomial-time algorithms under both pure and approximate differential privacy. Under pure $(\varepsilon,0)$-DP, we achieve $n = \widetilde O(k/(\alpha^2 m)+k/(\alpha\sqrt{m}\varepsilon)+k/\varepsilon)$, the first polynomial-time pure-DP guarantee matching the information-theoretic optimum up to logarithmic factors. Under approximate $(\varepsilon,\delta)$-DP, we achieve $n = \widetilde O(k/(\alpha^2 m)+k/(\alpha\sqrt{m}\varepsilon)+k+\log(1/\delta)/\varepsilon)$. At $\delta=2^{-\Theta(k)}$, this is $\widetilde O(k)$ for fixed $\alpha,\varepsilon,m$ and failure probability. Our algorithms use a new degree-6 sum-of-squares estimator for learning from untrusted batches. Its key ingredient is a trace-bounded diagonal majorizer for the difference between the empirical covariance of the repaired batch averages and the multinomial covariance predicted by their mean. We prove that clean data admit this certificate through semidefinite-programming duality and a new application of the stronger symmetric form of Grothendieck's inequality due to Friedland and Lim. The certificate preserves the mean-dependent variance of multinomial batch averages, yielding the near-optimal robust rate $O(\eta\sqrt{\log(1/\eta)/m})$ and providing the score required by the privacy reduction. We also prove a statistical query lower bound ruling out a uniformly smaller order of error under fixed polynomial SQ resource bounds.
item.dc:creator: Gautam Kamath, Mahbod Majid, Ankur Moitra, Argyris Mouzakis, Jonathan Ullman

item.title: Compressed Set Representations based on Set Difference
item.description: arXiv:2601.23240v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce a compressed representation of sets of sets that exploits how similar they are to each other. Our representation supports access, membership, predecessor and successor queries on the sets within logarithmic time. It also computes the support of any element (i.e., the sets containing it) in optimal time. In addition, we give a new MST-based construction algorithm for the representation that outperforms standard ones.
item.dc:creator: Travis Gagie, Meng He, Gonzalo Navarro

item.title: Fast Approximation Algorithms for Balanced Edge and Vertex Separators
item.description: arXiv:2603.15782v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a family of fast pseudo-approximation algorithms for the minimum balanced element cut problem in a graph, which includes vertex and edge separators. Given a graph $G=(V,E)$ with polynomially-bounded finite integer element weights with $n$ vertices and $m$ edges, and a (constant) balance parameter $c\in(0,1/2)$, where $G$ has some (unknown) $c$-balanced element cut of size $OPT_c$, we give a (Monte-Carlo randomized) algorithm running in $O(n^{\varepsilon}m^{1+o(1)})$ time that produces a $\Theta(1)$-balanced element cut of size $O(OPT_c\cdot\sqrt{(\log n)/\varepsilon})$ for any value $\varepsilon\in[\Theta(1/\log(n)),\Theta(1)]$. Our algorithms are based on a semidefinite programming (SDP) relaxation of the problem. A standard approach to solving an SDP relaxation for this kind of problem would use the primal-dual Matrix Multiplicative Weights Update framework of Arora and Kale, but this framework does not seem to apply, since we cannot express all of our SDPs primal variables explicitly. Instead, we present a new MMWU framework for our problem that allows us to represent some of our variables implicitly. We also extend our framework to a general "Partial-variable MMWU framework", which we expect will be useful for future work. Our oracle for the balanced element cut problem within our framework uses $O(n^{\varepsilon}\text{polylog}(n))$ almost-linear time maximum-flow computations, and would be sped up if the time complexity of maximum-flow improves. For graphs with padding bound $\beta$, another oracle gives an $O(\sqrt\beta/\varepsilon)$ approximation in $m^{1+o(1)}n^{\varepsilon}\operatorname{polylog}(n)$ time. It is known that $\beta\le O(\log h)$ for $K_h$-minor-free graphs (and in particular $\beta\le O(\log n)$).
item.dc:creator: Vladimir Kolmogorov, Jack Spalding-Jamieson

item.title: Optimal-Time Move Structure Construction
item.description: arXiv:2603.22147v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The move structure represents a permutation $\pi$ of $[0,n)$ by partitioning the domain into $O(r)$ disjoint, contiguously permuted intervals, with $r$ being the minimum number of such intervals. This data structure occupies $O(r)$ words of space and enables $O(1)$-time computation of $\pi(i)$ given the interval that contains $i$. For permutations where $r \ll n$, this provides an efficient, compressed representation for navigation. While the existing best $O(r)$-space construction approaches require $O(r\log r)$-time, we present an optimal $O(r)$-time and space construction algorithm. This is achieved by replacing balanced search trees with pointer-based lists through introducing a bidirectional strategy that synchronizes construction of the structures for $\pi$ and its inverse $\pi^{-1}$ in a single, unified pass. By applying this algorithm to an existing result, we achieve the first optimal $O(n)$-time construction of the longest common prefix (LCP) array from a run-length-encoded Burrows-Wheeler transform (RLBWT) of $r$ runs in $O(r)$ working space. Empirical evaluation on pangenome-scale data confirms that our move structure construction algorithm is consistently faster than the previous best, achieving speedups of up to $\sim 2\times$ while using less memory.
item.dc:creator: Nathaniel K. Brown, Ahsan Sanaullah, Shaojie Zhang, Ben Langmead

item.title: The Exact Approximation Ratio of the Optimal Fixed-Price Mechanism in Bilateral Trade
item.description: arXiv:2609.27878v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In bilateral trade, a seller owns an item that a buyer may value more, and their values are drawn independently from known distributions. A fixed-price mechanism posts a single price and trades exactly when both agents accept it. How much of the first-best expected welfare can the optimal fixed price guarantee? A sequence of analytic and computer-assisted results narrowed the worst-case ratio to the interval $[0.7292,0.73805]$, but its exact value remained open. We determine this ratio exactly: it equals $0.7380243357\ldots$, given in closed form through the unique root of an explicit one-dimensional equation. The guarantee holds for every pair of independent nonnegative distributions with finite means, including atomic and unbounded ones, and an explicit family of instances shows that no larger constant is possible. The proof reduces the problem, through put and call transforms of the two distributions and a worst-case choice of seller, to a one-dimensional control problem for the buyer. A logarithmic change of variables makes this problem strictly convex, so its first-order conditions certify a global optimum. The optimizer switches exactly once from an interior arc to the boundary and can be integrated in closed form. Realizing it yields a bounded seller and a bounded buyer together with a vanishing buyer atom at a diverging value. The worst case is approached by this family but attained by no instance.
item.dc:creator: Tao Jiang, Minbo Gao, Shaowei Cai

item.title: The Power of Flexible Budgets in Adwords
item.description: arXiv:2610.02479v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Search advertising platforms routinely spend beyond an advertiser's average daily budget on high-traffic days, so long as total spending over the month stays within the monthly budget. Motivated by this practice, we study a $D$-day generalization of the Adwords problem (Mehta et al. 2007), where each advertiser $i$ has a nominal (average) daily budget $B_i$ and a total horizon (monthly) budget $DB_i$. Given a flexibility parameter $\delta$, the platform may spend at most $\delta B_i$ on advertiser $i$ on any single day, subject to the horizon spending limit of $DB_i$. We quantify the power of $\delta$-flexible budgets by benchmarking against the inflexible offline optimum, which may spend at most $B_i$ on advertiser $i$ on each day. We show that no amount of flexibility helps direct generalizations of the classical algorithm of Mehta et al. (2007). By contrast, for every fixed $\delta$, we design an algorithm whose competitive ratio converges to $1-e^{-\delta}$ as $D\to\infty$, and we show that this is asymptotically optimal. Perhaps surprisingly, this matches the optimal competitive ratio in a more permissive setting where the algorithm receives a fresh spending limit of $\delta B_i$ each day and may spend up to $\delta D B_i$ over the horizon. Along the way, we characterize the exact optimal competitive ratio for every pair $(D,\delta)$ on high-traffic instances, where the offline benchmark exhausts every advertiser's budget on every day.
item.dc:creator: Suho Kang, Rajan Udwani

item.title: Incremental Exact Vertex Connectivity
item.description: arXiv:2610.21531v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the problem of maintaining the vertex connectivity $\kappa$ of a graph under edge insertions. For undirected graphs, our algorithm uses $O(\kappa^4 \log^2 n)$ amortized time per edge insertion. After each edge insertion, the algorithm outputs the current value of $\kappa$, plus a set of $\kappa$ vertices whose removal disconnects the graph. Our algorithm is Monte-Carlo randomized and works with a randomness-adaptive adversary. The algorithm also works on directed graphs against an oblivious adversary, which is equivalent to an output-adaptive adversary if we only have to output the current value of $\kappa$. Previously, algorithms using SPQR trees could maintain the vertex connectivity in undirected graphs with $O(\log n)$ time per edge insertion for $\kappa \le 3$, but no algorithm with $o(n)$ time per edge insertion was known for $\kappa \ge 4$. Moreover, for $\kappa \ge 4$, on general directed graphs or sparse undirected graphs, no algorithm faster than recomputation from scratch was known. We complement our algorithm with a conditional lower bound: Under the OMv conjecture, any insertions-only algorithm that outputs the current value of $\kappa$ after every insertion needs $\Omega(n^{1-\varepsilon})$ amortized time per edge insertion for $\kappa = \Theta(n)$. Previous conditional lower bounds for this problem only apply to worst case running time, or algorithms that support both edge insertions and edge deletions.
item.dc:creator: Felix Adena, Monika Henzinger, Christoph Kern, Daniel Rutschmann

item.title: NP-Completeness and ETH-Based Additive Inapproximability of Deterministic Communication Complexity via Relaxed Interlacing
item.description: arXiv:2508.05597v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: How difficult is it to find an efficient communication protocol when the entire truth table of the function is given? We give a unified interlacing proof of NP-completeness for exact optimisation and of hardness of approximation. Assuming the Exponential Time Hypothesis, there is a computable, nondecreasing additive error allowance tending to infinity for which approximation is impossible in polynomial time. The proof uses interlacing, which asks the players to solve one problem selected by Alice from a collection of inputs held by Bob. For suitable matrices, a short protocol must reveal enough of Alice's selection to encode a solution to a combinatorial problem. This produces a one-bit communication gap in a polynomial-size matrix and proves exact hardness. Repeating the construction is harder: earlier messages can remove the inputs on which a later lower bound depends. Restriction bounds that survive the construction make the one-bit gain repeatable. A smaller, balanced family of interlaced columns controls the truth-table size. For every fixed number of applications, the construction takes subexponential time in the source length. This rules out every fixed additive error under ETH. A general computability argument then yields the stated unbounded allowance.
item.dc:creator: Serge Gaspers, Tao Zixu He, Simon Mackenzie

item.title: Fast and Compact Graph Cuts for the Boykov-Kolmogorov Algorithm
item.description: arXiv:2605.13402v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Computing a minimum $s$-$t$ cut in a graph is a solution to a wide range of computer vision problems and is often done using the Boykov-Kolmogorov (BK) algorithm. In this paper, we revisit the BK algorithm from both a theoretical and practical point of view. We improve the analysis of the time complexity of the BK algorithm to $O(mn|C|)$ and propose a new algorithm, the fast BK (fBK) algorithm, with a time complexity of $O(m|C|)$, where $m$, $n$, and $|C|$ are the number of edges, the number of vertices, and the capacity of the cut, respectively. We additionally propose a compact graph representation that allows our implementations of the BK and fBK algorithms to find a minimum $s$-$t$ cut in a graph with up to $10^9$ vertices and $10^{10}$ edges on a machine with 128 GB of memory. We denote these as $\texttt{cBK}$ and $\texttt{fcBK}$, respectively. Despite $\texttt{fcBK}$ having the better worst-case guarantee, we find $\texttt{cBK}$ to be the fastest available implementation within the family of BK algorithms when evaluating on a comprehensive set of benchmark datasets, highlighting the importance of memory-efficient implementations. We make our implementations publicly available for further research and implementation development within minimum $s$-$t$ cut algorithms.
item.dc:creator: Christian M{\o}ller Mikkelstrup, Anders Bjorholm Dahl, Philip Bille, Vedrana Andersen Dahl, Inge Li G{\o}rtz
